trial.title: Harnessing Neuroplasticity to Enhance Functional Recovery During Chronic Recovery From Upper Extremity Nerve Repair

endpoints.measure: Change from Baseline Dellon Modified Moberg Pick-Up Test performance at two weeks.
endpoints.time_frame: Baseline, immediately after end of intervention (+/- 3 days).
endpoints.description: This functional test measures quality of sensibility of the hand. This outcome measure will investigate any change in participant performance between pre- and post-intervention sessions of the Dellon Modified Moberg Pick-Up Test.

endpoints.measure: Change from Baseline Action Research Arm Test (ARAT) performance at two weeks.
endpoints.time_frame: Baseline, immediately after end of intervention (+/- 3 days).
endpoints.description: The Action Research Arm Test (ARAT) measures limb function by having participants pick up various objects of different sizes, different weights, and different shapes (e.g., a glass of water, a cricket ball). This secondary outcome measure will investigate any change in participant performance between pre- and post-intervention sessions of the ARAT.

endpoints.measure: Change from baseline upper limb movement as measured by actigraphy-derived variables during everyday life at periodic intervals after intervention.
endpoints.time_frame: Baseline, post intervention at week 1, post intervention at 1 month, post intervention at 3 months, post intervention at 6 months.
endpoints.description:
This secondary outcome measure will employ actigraphy on participants to measure limb movement in everyday life before and after the intervention. Participants will wear wrist-watch like devices that contain accelerometers on each upper extremity in 24-72 hour sessions. Two primary variables will quantify upper limb activity from accelerometer data: the Bilateral Magnitude and the Magnitude Ratio. The Bilateral Magnitude quantifies the intensity of activity across both limbs, whereas the Magnitude Ratio quantifies the contribution of each limb to activity.

This outcome measure will investigate the change in the Bilateral Magnitude and Magnitude Ratio between a baseline pre-intervention test and post-intervention actigraphy sessions performed within one week of completion of the intervention, at 1 month post-intervention, 3-months post intervention, and 6-months post intervention.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT03610763 evaluates bi-hemispheric tDCS combined with modified CIMT for chronic-stage hand function recovery after hand transplantation, replantation, or peripheral nerve repair. Population: adults 12-18 months post-surgery with plateaued recovery. Primary endpoint: Dellon Modified Moberg Pick-Up Test change at 2 weeks. Secondary endpoints: ARAT at 2 weeks; actigraphy-derived Bilateral Magnitude and Magnitude Ratio at multiple timepoints.

Evidence search retrieved literature on tDCS+CIMT in stroke (indirect population), peripheral nerve injury outcomes, and actigraphy validation. No direct evidence for this specific combination in hand transplantation/replantation/nerve repair patients. Retrieved studies on tDCS+rehabilitation in stroke show small-to-moderate effect sizes for motor function. CIMT alone shows established efficacy in chronic stroke. Combined tDCS+CIMT pilot studies in chronic stroke suggest additive benefits.

Evidence role assessment: tDCS+CIMT studies in stroke (chronic upper limb dysfunction) provide indirect_direction evidence for motor function improvement, but population mismatch (stroke vs. peripheral nerve injury/transplantation) limits numeric use. Peripheral nerve injury literature confirms functional recovery plateaus at 12-18 months, supporting the rationale for intervention timing. Actigraphy validation studies support the measurement approach but provide no specific effect estimates.

Key uncertainties: (1) No published trials of tDCS+CIMT specifically in hand transplantation, replantation, or peripheral nerve repair; (2) Chronic peripheral nerve injury may have different neuroplasticity potential than stroke; (3) Sensibility outcomes (Moberg) may respond differently than motor outcomes; (4) Small sample sizes in pilot studies limit precision; (5) Expected completion date 2025-06-01 means results are not yet available.

Safety considerations: tDCS at 1.5mA is generally well-tolerated with mild adverse effects (skin irritation, headache). No serious safety signals expected. CIMT is established rehabilitation with manageable fatigue/discomfort risks.

Prediction rationale: Based on indirect evidence from stroke literature showing tDCS+CIMT produces small-to-moderate motor improvements, and mechanistic rationale for neuroplasticity enhancement in chronic recovery, the intervention is likely to produce measurable but modest improvements in motor function (ARAT) and real-world activity (actigraphy). Sensibility outcomes (Moberg) have weaker mechanistic support from tDCS and may show smaller effects. Confidence is low-to-moderate due to population mismatch and lack of direct evidence.
